accuracy.evidence: Dates checked: Heroic Age 1897–1922 (Belgica to Shackleton's death on Quest); Amundsen left Framheim 19 Oct 1911 and reached the Pole 14 Dec 1911 (56 days); back at Framheim 26 Jan 1912 after 99 days and about 3,000 km travelled (Fram Museum), so about 1,500 km each way, about 27 km a day; news cabled from Hobart 7 Mar 1912; 1,500 km at 300 km/h = 5 h. First GPS satellite 1978, Sputnik 1957, Byrd's South Pole flight 1929, Halley VI opened 2013, dogs removed under the Madrid Protocol by April 1994, first women at the South Pole 12 Nov 1969 (Lois Jones's team), Antarctic Treaty 1959 with 50+ parties, Scott's party's ~16 kg of Beardmore Glacier rocks with Glossopteris fossils. CO2 ~280 ppm in 1800, ~190 ppm at the Last Glacial Maximum, below 300 ppm through the EPICA Dome C 800,000-year record, 420+ ppm today.

misconceptions.evidence: Predictions target documented slips: that 1911 teams could radio home, that the sledge trip took days rather than 8 weeks, that Heroic Age explorers did no science, that deeper ice is younger, and that women only recently went to the Pole. Each sort card's wrong drop explains the specific date that rules it out (GPS 1978, satellites 1957, plane over the Pole 1929, dogs out by 1994).

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is about this topic's own contrast: kit dated to the Heroic Age or today, a time slider that runs a 56-day sledge against a 5-hour ski plane over the same route, old science questions matched to modern tools, an ice-core drill whose samples must be put in age order with their CO2 values, and team facts then vs now. It shares no mechanic with flagpolex (race calendar, cold-kit packing, Endurance story) or flagarctic.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners discover the scale of change by dragging time (days vs hours), discover that age increases with depth by drilling and ordering samples, and discover that the questions stayed the same while the tools changed by giving each old question its new tool; the step text then names the idea.

predictions.evidence: Five locked predictions each with a tempting wrong option: 'He radioed from the Pole', 'About 56 days' for the plane, 'No, they only raced', 'younger than the top', and '2020' for women at the Pole. The lab task after each prediction shows the answer and A.reveal reports whether the prediction was right.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions; every wrong option carries its own tag with a specific correction (dogs, sext, radio, sat, young, same, race, one, men, tent), e.g. 'No radio went on the trek. The news went by ship to Hobart, then by telegraph in March 1912.'

readability.evidence: Kid explanation FK grade 1.8 and adult 9.0 by learn/readability.py (limits 6.5 and 9.5); short sentences and plain words, with sextant, ice core and research station explained where they first appear.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph carries facts or a check: kit, risk, modern tools, ice cores, teams. No filler phrases (gate_content regexes pass); no repeated template text between steps.

mobile.evidence: Canvas switches to a taller ratio under 520 px; sort card and bins are full-width with large hit areas, the time slider has a 32 px tall grab band, and every action also has a full-size button below the canvas; checked on iPhone 13 screenshots.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag or tap has a button (bin buttons, traveller buttons, time +25%, tool buttons, Drill deeper, sample buttons); the canvas aria-label is updated with the full state after every action; axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark themes on desktop and phone (walk.cjs).
